name: toast
purpose: A transient, non-blocking notification system: mount the `<Toaster>` region **once** near the application root, then raise notifications imperatively from anywhere via the exported `toast()` function (`toast('Saved')`) and its type shortcuts (`toast.success`, `toast.error`, `toast.info`, `toast.warning`, `toast.loading`, `toast.promise`, `toast.dismiss`). Each notification is a self-dismissing card that stacks in a corner, animates in and out, and is announced to assistive technology — without stealing focus. Unlike the sibling [`Alert`](alert.md), which is an **inline** banner the consumer places in the document flow and controls with `v-model`-style props, Toast is a **transient overlay** stack driven by an imperative call and a shared reactive store, so the call site needs no local visibility state and no markup of its own. The card surface, typography, and severity icons follow the Figma design (see `figma` in the frontmatter). The interaction model follows the established mount-once toast pattern (a single anchored region + imperative trigger + auto-dismiss stack that groups collapsed and expands on hover), built on our tokens, our semantic animation utilities, and our composition/compound-API conventions per [`.claude/rules/migration.md`](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.claude/rules/migration.md); nothing is inherited from any external library. Each severity tints only its leading **icon** via the matching `-contrast` token (`var(--success-contrast)` / `var(--warning-contrast)` / `var(--danger-contrast)` / `var(--info-contrast)`) over the shared `var(--bg-surface-raised)` surface.
setup: One-time app-level wiring before the first toast() call — service (recommended): import { ToastPlugin } from '@aziontech/webkit/toast' and chain .use(ToastPlugin) onto createApp() in the app entry; the plugin mounts the toast region automatically. Alternative: mount a Toaster component once near the app root. `webkit doctor` flags toast usage with no wired region.
useWhen: Confirming the result of an action that finished out of view or in the background: saved, deployed, copied.
Following an async operation from start to finish with `toast.promise`, or `toast.loading` plus a dismiss by id.
A short notice that is not tied to one place on the page and can disappear on its own.
avoidWhen: The message must stay visible next to the content it concerns → use `message`.
The user must decide something before continuing → use `dialog`.
Validation feedback for a single field → use `helper-text`.
related: message` — inline severity banner placed in the page flow; it stays until it is closed.
dialog` — blocking modal for decisions and confirmations.
spinner` — rendered by the `loading` toast type.
bestPractices: Mount `Toaster` once near the app root, or install `ToastPlugin`. Don't mount one per page; the store renders only the first registered region.

Use the typed shortcuts (`toast.success`, `toast.error`, …). The type sets the icon and the live-region urgency: `error` makes the region assertive, and `error` and `warning` items get `role="alert"`.

Keep the message text to one line and move detail to `description`. Offer at most two actions: one `action`, or `actions` with two entries when a failure has two ways forward (**Edit** and **Redeploy**).
duration: 0` keeps a toast until it is dismissed. Keep the returned id and call `toast.dismiss(id)`, or pass the same `id` to update the toast in place.
Don't make a toast the only path to an important action. It auto-dismisses and never takes focus.

props.name: position
props.doc: Corner (or edge-center) the stack is anchored to.

props.name: duration
props.doc: Default auto-dismiss time in ms each toast inherits; a per-toast `duration` overrides it, and `0` keeps the toast until dismissed.

props.name: max
props.doc: Maximum simultaneously visible toasts per corner before the rest queue behind.

props.name: expand
props.doc: Lay the stack out fully expanded with a gap; when `false` the resting stack overlaps into a peek.

props.name: closable
props.doc: Show an always-visible close control on every toast; a per-toast `closable` option overrides it.

slots.name: default
slots.notes: Optional override for a single toast's body. `toast` is the store entry (`{ id, type, message, description?, action?, actions?, duration }`); `dismiss` dismisses that entry. When omitted, the `Toaster` composes `ToastItem` + `Title`/`Description`/`Action`/`Close` from the entry, rendering one `Action` per entry of `actions` (the first two) or the single `action`.

examples.name: Default
examples.sfc:
<script setup>
  import { Toaster, toast } from '@aziontech/webkit/toast'
  import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'

  const show = () =>
    toast('Event has been created', {
      description: 'Sunday, December 03, 2023 at 9:00 AM',
      action: { label: 'Undo', onClick: () => {} }
    })
</script>

<template>
  <Toaster position="bottom-right" />
  <Button
    label="Show toast"
    @click="show"
  />
</template>
